newsitem.title: UK: ASDA up, SBC Warburg says "buy' up to 130p.
newsitem.headline: ASDA up, SBC Warburg says "buy' up to 130p.

text.p: Shares in ASDA Group Plc were slightly higher on Friday in active trade as analysts at SBC Warburg and SGST repeated their positive stance on the stock.
The shares were up 1-1/4p at 112p by 1217 GMT and were the most actively traded of the day in volume of 9.6 million shares.
Other supermarket stocks also benefited from positive analyst comment on the sector as a whole.
Shares in Safeway were up 1/2p at 342-1/2p and Tesco was unchanged at 302p in a generally weaker stock market and after a 9p fall on Thursday.
Shares in Sainsbury's edged 1/2p lower to 390p.
"We are recommending an overweight position in the sector," said Andrew Kasoulis, a food retail analyst at SBC Warburg.
"The fall in ASDA's share price since the appointment of Archie Norman as chairman has been enough," he added.
"On a short term 6-12 month view the stock is still cheap and we've got a 130p price target on it," Kasoulis said.
ASDA shares have lost 9p over the last seven days. Analysts at SGST also reiterated their positive stance on the stock.
